name: bKlug Floating Contact Button
author: bKlug AI

sections.description:
bKlug Floating Contact Button puts a WhatsApp chat on every page of your WordPress site, with no theme editing and no code. Set your number in the settings and the button appears. Fill in one number to send visitors straight into a chat, or add several and let them choose who to reach. Want the conversation to start with context? Switch on the ask-a-question bar and the visitor’s question rides into WhatsApp as the very first message, so you never open with “hi”.

Key features

  • 💬 Floating WhatsApp button: One-tap chat from any page, bottom-left or bottom-right. Icon only, or icon plus a label you choose.
  • ✍️ Ask-a-question bar: A centered bar visitors type into. Their question becomes the first WhatsApp message, so the chat starts with context. On a computer they scan a QR code to continue on their phone; on a phone WhatsApp opens straight away.
  • 👥 Up to five contacts, with a picker: Give sales, support, or each store its own number, name, note, and pre-filled message. Two or more numbers open a clean contact picker so visitors choose who to message.
  • 💡 Suggested questions: Offer up to three one-tap question chips to get the conversation moving.
  • 🕒 Business hours: Show a live “available now” or “away” note with a status dot, based on the current time, days, and time zone.
  • 👋 Auto-open nudge: Optionally open the contact picker after a visitor has been idle for a set time, so the nudge lands in a pause rather than mid-read.
  • 🎨 Full styling control: Colours for the button, the WhatsApp mark, the contact cards, and the bar, plus size and spacing. Show or hide on desktop and mobile independently.
  • 🔒 Fast and private: Lightweight, framework-free JavaScript that loads only on pages where the button appears. No account required, and no visitor data leaves your site.

Nothing is answered on your site and nothing is stored. Every conversation happens in WhatsApp, where your customers already are, and it starts with everything you need to reply. A free tool from bKlug.

This plugin bundles qrcode-generator by Kazuhiko Arase (MIT licensed) to draw QR codes in the browser. No QR service is contacted and the code is generated entirely on the visitor’s device.

This plugin uses WhatsApp’s standard wa.me links. WhatsApp is a trademark of its respective owner, and this plugin is not affiliated with or endorsed by WhatsApp or Meta.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the bklug-floating-contact-button folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install the plugin through the Plugins screen in WordPress.
  2. Activate the plugin through the “Plugins” screen.
  3. Go to Settings → bKlug Contact Button.
  4. Enter at least one WhatsApp number (including the country code) and save.
  5. Visit the front end of your site and the floating button appears.
sections.faq:
Do I need a WhatsApp Business account?

No. The button opens a standard WhatsApp chat to whatever number you enter. A personal or Business number both work.

Why doesn’t the button show up?

The button only appears once at least one WhatsApp number is set in Settings → bKlug Contact Button. Also check that “Show on desktop” / “Show on mobile” are enabled for the device you are testing.

What number format should I use?

Include the country code, for example +1 555 123 1234. Spaces, dashes, and the plus sign are fine. The plugin strips them automatically.

Do not use a national format. WhatsApp reads the digits as an international number, so a number entered as (11) 98765-4321 or 011 98765-4321 will open a chat with whoever those digits belong to somewhere else in the world. The settings screen warns you if a number looks like it is missing its country code.

Can I show more than one number?

Yes. Fill in up to five contacts. With two or more, the button opens a contact picker so visitors choose who to message.

Does it slow down my site?

No. The CSS and JavaScript are small, framework-free, and only load on pages where the button is displayed. The QR code generator is a separate file that is only downloaded if a visitor actually submits a question, so ordinary page views never pay for it.

Does the ask-a-question bar answer questions on my site?

No. It collects the question and carries it into WhatsApp as the first message, so you answer in WhatsApp as usual. The wording under the field says so, and you can edit it in the settings.

Does it still work outside my business hours?

Yes. Nothing is hidden outside business hours. Only the note changes. Questions still reach WhatsApp and wait for you there.
sections.changelog:
1.1.5

  • Fixed: the auto-open setting is now hidden unless two or more WhatsApp numbers are set, matching the behavior 1.1.4 gave the button itself. Since 1.1.4 the button correctly never opened on its own with a single number, but the setting stayed on screen and could still be switched on and saved, where it did nothing.
  • Fixed: the auto-open help text said that with a single number the menu would show just that one number. That has not been true since 1.1.4. It now says the menu needs at least two numbers. Updated in all four translations.

1.1.4

  • Fixed: with a single WhatsApp number set, the button no longer opens a contact card on its own. One number is now always a one-tap direct link to WhatsApp that stays still until the visitor taps it. Auto-open now applies only when two or more numbers are set. This reverses the single-number auto-open behavior introduced in 1.1.1.

1.1.3

  • Listing update only: refreshed the description and added new screenshots of the ask-a-question bar. No changes to the plugin code.

1.1.2

  • Fixed: a question that had already been sent stayed in the box after closing, so the collapsed bar showed it back to the visitor and the send button beside it would send the same question again. A question you have not sent yet is still kept, so closing the bar by accident does not lose what you were typing.
  • Fixed: closing the ask-a-question bar left a white card, with its shadow, painted around the collapsed bar for a moment.
  • The ask-a-question bar now resizes smoothly between all of its screens, in both directions: opening, sending, showing and hiding the QR code, and closing. Previously each screen appeared at its new size in a single frame. Respects the “reduce motion” accessibility setting.

1.1.1

  • Fixed: the close button on the ask-a-question bar did not close it. Pressing it reopened the bar in the same click, so the bar could only be dismissed by clicking elsewhere on the page or pressing Escape.
  • Fixed: auto-open did nothing when only one WhatsApp number was set, and the setting was hidden in that case. Switching it on now gives the single number a contact card to open, and the setting is offered for any round button.
  • The auto-open delay is now labelled “Idle time before it opens”, which is what it has always measured: scrolling or moving the mouse restarts it, so the nudge lands in a pause rather than mid-read.
  • Contacts no longer arrive pre-filled. Contact 1 and 2 used to ship with a display name and subheading already written in, so filling in only a number published wording you never chose. The examples now live in the help text under each field.

1.1.0

  • New “Ask-a-question bar” button display: a centered bar visitors type a question into. The question is carried into WhatsApp as the first message.
  • On desktop the bar shows a QR code to scan with a phone; on mobile it deep-links straight into WhatsApp.
  • Added up to three suggested questions, shown as tappable chips.
  • The bar centres itself at the bottom of the screen; round buttons keep their corner.
  • Choose separately what phones get: the bar, or a round button.
  • Business hours accept a named time zone or a manual UTC offset.
  • Bundles qrcode-generator 2.0.4 by Kazuhiko Arase (MIT), loaded on demand only when a visitor submits a question.

1.0.0

  • Initial release.
